2026-05-27.name: Kochi
2026-05-27.text: On May 27, 2014, Kerala Blasters FC was formed as one of the original clubs of the Indian Super League. Kochi soon became synonymous with the club's bright yellow identity and the roaring Manjappada supporters who helped make it one of the most visible stories in modern Indian football.

2026-05-27.name: Golden Gate Bridge
2026-05-27.text: On May 27, 1937, the Golden Gate Bridge opened to the public and immediately became the signature sight of San Francisco Bay. At the time it had the world's longest suspension bridge span, turning a foggy strait into one of the best-known views in modern engineering.

2026-05-27.name: Le Mans
2026-05-27.text: On May 27, 1923, the first 24 Hours of Le Mans began and introduced a race built around endurance rather than pure speed. Since then, the city has become a permanent shorthand for all-night driving, mechanical survival, and motorsport prestige.

2026-05-27.name: Centralia
2026-05-27.text: On May 27, 1962, a fire at a landfill in Centralia spread into an abandoned coal mine and began the underground blaze that still burns today. The Pennsylvania town became famous for a disaster measured not in hours or days, but in generations of smoke, heat, and abandonment.

2026-05-27.name: Old Parliament House
2026-05-27.text: On May 27, Australia begins National Reconciliation Week on the anniversary of the 1967 referendum on Indigenous Australians. Old Parliament House stands close to the political world in which that vote reshaped the country's constitutional story and remains a powerful symbol of public debate in Canberra.

2026-05-28.name: Red Square
2026-05-28.text: On May 28, 1987, West German pilot Mathias Rust slipped through Soviet air defences and landed near Red Square. The improbable flight stunned the world and exposed deep embarrassment inside one of the Cold War's most guarded states.

2026-05-28.name: Mantua
2026-05-28.text: On May 28, 1608, Claudio Monteverdi premiered L'Arianna in Mantua during lavish wedding festivities for the Gonzaga court. Almost all of the opera has since vanished, leaving the city attached to one of music history's most famous lost masterpieces.

2026-05-28.name: Meskel Square
2026-05-28.text: On May 28, Ethiopia marks the Downfall of the Derg, the 1991 collapse of the military regime that had ruled the country for years. Meskel Square in Addis Ababa has long been one of the capital's great stages for state ceremony and public feeling, making it closely tied to national turning points.

2026-05-28.name: Chagai Hills
2026-05-28.text: On May 28, 1998, Pakistan conducted the Chagai-I nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills and thrust this remote desert landscape into global headlines. The barren hills became a defining image in South Asia's nuclear history almost overnight.

2026-05-28.name: Oakland
2026-05-28.text: On May 28, 1892, John Muir founded the Sierra Club, helping turn conservation into an organized public cause. Oakland later became closely associated with that legacy as the longtime home of one of the world's best-known environmental organizations.

2026-05-29.name: Hawthorne Bridge
2026-05-29.text: On May 29, 2011, Portland residents gathered on Hawthorne Bridge for Hands Across Hawthorne after an attack on a same-sex couple. For a day, the bridge became a public symbol of solidarity rather than traffic, linking a local landmark to a broader argument about safety and dignity in public space.

2026-05-29.name: N'Djamena
2026-05-29.text: On May 29, 1900, the settlement that became N'Djamena was founded as Fort-Lamy by French commander Emile Gentil. The capital later shed its colonial name, so the date connects today's city to a very different era of empire and administration.

2026-05-29.name: Theatre des Champs-Elysees
2026-05-29.text: On May 29, 1913, the premiere of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees caused one of the most famous uproars in music history. Paris suddenly found itself arguing over pounding rhythms and angular choreography that would later look like the arrival of modernism.

2026-05-29.name: Sardarabad
2026-05-29.text: On May 29, 1918, Armenian forces prevailed at Sardarabad in a battle remembered as crucial to the survival of the Armenian nation. The name of this small place carries the weight of a much larger story about resistance, statehood, and historical memory.

2026-05-29.name: Castleton
2026-05-29.text: On May 29, Castleton in Derbyshire keeps Oak Apple Day alive through Garland Day, when a rider hidden beneath a towering cone of flowers circles the village. It is one of England's most visually distinctive local customs, equal parts pageant, folklore, and floral engineering.

2026-05-30.name: Auckland Harbour Bridge
2026-05-30.text: On May 30, 1959, the Auckland Harbour Bridge officially opened across Waitemata Harbour. It quickly became one of New Zealand's defining urban landmarks, physically joining parts of Auckland that the water had long kept apart.

2026-05-30.name: Lincoln Memorial
2026-05-30.text: On May 30, 1922, the Lincoln Memorial was dedicated in Washington, D.C., giving the American capital one of its most recognizable civic spaces. It later became a national stage for speeches, protest, and remembrance far beyond its original role as a monument to one president.

2026-05-30.name: Kota Kinabalu
2026-05-30.text: On May 30, Kaamatan begins across Sabah, and Kota Kinabalu becomes one of the festival's best-known urban stages. The harvest celebration brings together rice traditions, music, dance, and regional identity from across Malaysian Borneo.

2026-05-30.name: The Valley
2026-05-30.text: On May 30, Anguilla Day commemorates the opening of the Anguillian Revolution in 1967. The Valley, the island's tiny capital, sits at the center of a constitutional story much larger than its size suggests.

2026-05-30.name: Santa Cruz de Tenerife
2026-05-30.text: On May 30, the Canary Islands celebrate their regional day, marking the first session of the islands' parliament in 1983. Santa Cruz de Tenerife is closely tied to the observance as one of the archipelago's capitals and the home of its parliament.

2026-05-31.name: Ulm Minster
2026-05-31.text: On May 31, 1890, Ulm Minster was completed after centuries of construction, securing its claim as the tallest church building in the world. Its immense spire turned the city into a landmark of persistence in stone and skyline ambition.

2026-05-31.name: Vereeniging
2026-05-31.text: On May 31, 1902, the Treaty of Vereeniging ended the Second Boer War. The town's name has been linked to that agreement ever since, tying one South African place to a major turning point in imperial history.

2026-05-31.name: Surabaya
2026-05-31.text: On May 31, 1293, a Majapahit victory over the Mongol invasion of Java became the traditional founding date of Surabaya. The city still carries that origin story, along with the famous shark-and-crocodile legend often used to explain its name.

2026-05-31.name: Biblioteca Marciana
2026-05-31.text: On May 31, 1468, Cardinal Bessarion donated 746 manuscripts to the Republic of Venice, an act regarded as the foundation of the Biblioteca Marciana. The library still reflects Venice's role in carrying Greek learning into the world of Renaissance humanism.

2026-05-31.name: Gold Coast
2026-05-31.text: On May 31, Borobi Day recalls the legacy of the 2018 Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast through school sport and mascot-themed events. A bright blue koala is an unusual way for a city to remember an international sporting festival, which is exactly why the date sticks in memory.
